en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa-kanda
5. The Training Rule on Receiving Food At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā was beautiful, pleasing to behold, and inspiring.
When people saw the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā in the dining hall, being lustful themselves, they gave the finest foods to the lustful bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā.
The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā ate as much as she desired,
while the other bhikkhunīs did not receive what they wished for.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can the noble lady Sundarīnandā, being lustful, accept with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man and eat it? ... [The Buddha asked:
"Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, accepts with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man and eats it?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, accept with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man and then eat it?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule as follows:
‘Whatever bhikkhunī, being lustful, [accepts] fresh or cooked food from the hand of a lustful man—’”
Or if she, having received it with her own hand, should eat or consume it, this nun too has committed an offense that is an immediate offense,
a *saṅghādisesa*, which entails formal meeting and expulsion.
"Whoever" means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
"Passionate" means being enamored,
full of longing, and having a mind bound [to another].
"The passionate one" means...
One who is lustful, full of longing, and whose mind is bound.
A "person" (purisapuggala) means a human being, not a *yakkha*, not a *peta*, nor an animal; one who is wise and capable of becoming lustful.
“Hard food” means:
excluding the five kinds of cooked food, water, and tooth-sticks, the remainder is called “hard food. “Soft food” means: [the five kinds of cooked food].
There are five kinds of food: boiled rice, sour gruel, flour, fish, and meat.
If one receives them with the intention, "I will chew it" or "I will eat it," there is a grave offense (thullaccaya).
For every swallow, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
This too is said in reference to the preceding [offenses].
"An offense of the first entanglement" (paṭhamāpatti) means:
One incurs [this offense] together with the transgression of the matter itself through failure to have her formally admonished.
"Leading to expulsion" means she is expelled from the Saṅgha.
"Saṅghādisesa": ...
[as before] ... for that reason also it is called "saṅghādisesa.
If one accepts water or a tooth-stick, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one who is alone and lustful accepts [food] with the intention, "I will chew it, I will eat it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of serious transgression (thullaccaya).
If he accepts water or a tooth-stick, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If one receives from the hand of a person who is lustful toward both [sexes], or a *yakkha*, or a *peta*, or a *paṇḍaka*, or one with the form of a human animal, thinking, "I will eat it; I will consume it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
For every swallow, there is an offense of serious transgression (*thullaccaya*).
If one receives water or a tooth-stick, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one who is already satisfied on one side accepts [food] thinking, "I will eat it," "I will consume it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one accepts water or a tooth-stick, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if both are free from lust,
or if she accepts it knowing that he is free from lust.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of a first-offender.
The fifth Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.
